",["$","code",null,{"children":"s"}]," and ",["$","code",null,{"children":"t"}],", count the number of **distinct subsequences of ",["$","code",null,{"children":"s"}]," that equal ",["$","code",null,{"children":"t**"}],". This breaks from the LCS-style problems above — it's no longer symmetric between the two strings. ",["$","code",null,{"children":"t"}]," must be matched ",["$","strong",null,{"children":"in full and in order"}],"; only ",["$","code",null,{"children":"s"}]," gets to \"skip\" characters."]}],"\n",["$","p",null,{"children":[["$","strong",null,{"children":"Recursion tree"}]," (example: ",["$","code",null,{"children":"s = \"babgbag\""}]," truncated to ",["$","code",null,{"children":"s = \"bag\""}],", ",["$","code",null,{"children":"t = \"bg\""}],"; = min pieces to partition s[i:] into palindromes\n     = min over every j >= i, where s[i..j] IS a palindrome, of:  1 + f(j+1)\n                                                                    ↑ one piece (s[i..j]) + best for the rest\nf(n) = 0                                        ← empty suffix needs 0 pieces (base case)\n\nanswer = f(0) - 1                               ← (pieces - 1) = cuts between them\n"}]}],"\n",["$","p",null,{"children":[["$","strong",null,{"children":"Recursion tree"}]," (example: ",["$","code",null,{"children":"s = \"aab\""}],", ",["$","code",null,{"children":"n = 3"}],"; state ",["$","code",null,{"children":"f(i)"}]," = min pieces for ",["$","code",null,{"children":"s[i:]"}],", target ",["$","code",null,{"children":"f(0)"}],"):"]}],"\n",["$","pre",null,{"children":["$","code",null,{"children":"                                    f(0)                    try every end j = 0, 1, 2 for 1 + f(1)      1 + f(2)\n                            |              |\n                    j=1:\"a\"(pal) only   j=2:\"b\"(pal) only\n                       1 + f(2)             1 + f(3)\n                            |                   |\n                        f(2)=1              f(3)=0  ← base case (empty suffix)\n                    (from \"b\" + f(3))\n\n        f(2) = 1 + f(3) = 1\n        f(1) = 1 + f(2) = 2        (only \"a\" is a valid first piece; \"ab\" isn't a palindrome)\n        f(0) = min(1 + f(1), 1 + f(2)) = min(1+2, 1+1) = 2\n\n        answer = f(0) - 1 = 1 cut   →  \"aa\" | ",["$","code",null,{"children":"arr = [1,15"}]]}],"\n",["$","p",null,{"children":[["$","code",null,{"children":"DP ,7]"}],", ",["$","code",null,{"children":"k = 2"}]," → chunk it as ",["$","code",null,{"children":"[1] | [15,7]"}],": the second chunk becomes ",["$","code",null,{"children":"[15,15]"}],", total ",["$","code",null,{"children":"= 1 + 15 + 15 = 31"}],"... but trying ",["$","code",null,{"children":"[1,15] | [7]"}]," gives ",["$","code",null,{"children":"15+15+7 = 37"}],", which is better — you have to search over chunk boundaries to find the best one."]}],"\n",["$","p",null,{"children":[["$","strong",null,{"children":"Same shape as Palindrome Partitioning II, one index, no second half."}]," Fix where the ",["$","strong",null,{"children":"first chunk"}]," ends, and everything after it is an independent copy of the same problem — so again the state is just one suffix index, ",["$","code",null,{"children":"f(ind)"}]," = best possible sum for ",["$","code",null,{"children":"arr[ind:]"}],". ",["$","code",null,{"children":"n"}],"."]}],"\n",["$","pre",null,{"children":["$","code",null,{"children":"f(ind) = best sum achievable for arr[ind:]\n       = max over chunk length L = 1..k (while                    ← nothing left, contributes 0 (base case)\n\nanswer = f(0)\n"}]}],"\n",["$","p",null,{"children":["Notice the inner loop ",["$","strong",null,{"children":"grows the chunk one
